issues.description: Example uses gratuitous `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` where indexing would do
issues.detail: The basic-usage example retrieves a node via `next(n for n in pipeline.nodes)` — obscure, order-dependent, and equivalent to `pipeline.nodes[0]` written badly. Copy-pasted into user code this becomes cargo cult. Use indexing, or state the invariant if nodes isn't indexable.

issues.description: ImagePreview example has unreachable code after `return`
issues.detail: The data-URI alternative is shown as a commented-out block placed after the `return` statement. A reader skimming sees two returns; one is dead. Split into two named functions or parameterize. Docs should not teach sloppy control flow by example.

issues.description: `meta` field complects renderer config with descriptive metadata under one name
issues.detail: The same `meta` dict carries Mermaid renderer config and CSS `textStyle` alongside arbitrary user metadata like timestamps and versions. The doc later admits meta has 'two purposes' — one too many. The schema conflates rendering directives with value metadata and forces readers to guess which keys are reserved.

issues.description: Closure-capture pattern shown without warning about binding hazard and frozen-at-construction semantics
issues.detail: The `make_preview_fn` example captures `sample_data` by reference at pipeline-construction time and presents this as the 'data context' pattern. Docs never warn that mutation after construction silently alters preview output, nor clarify that the snapshot is frozen even though preview is invoked later. Both the footgun and the time/identity semantics need to be named.

issues.description: preview_fn contract and failure semantics are unspecified
issues.detail: The docs introduce `preview_fn` as 'a callable that returns a preview payload' without stating purity, side-effect, idempotency, or failure semantics. The 'best practices' section then papers over the gap with 'wrap in try-except if needed' — defensive advice substituted for a real contract. Callers cannot reason about what preview() guarantees.

issues.description: Example snippets use `...` literals and reference undefined functions, so they don't run as written
issues.detail: CustomPreview shows `"nodes": [...]` / `"edges": [...]` which serialize to Ellipsis, and Mermaid/Text snippets call `process_data` and `calculate_metrics` with no imports or definitions. Either make examples self-contained and runnable, or clearly mark them as fragments.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a documentation patch that is broadly useful but ships several teach-by-bad-example problems and one underspecified contract. The strongest cross-reviewer signals: the `next(... for ...)` retrieval and the post-return dead code in ImagePreview were independently flagged as sloppy patterns that propagate; the `meta` field conflates renderer config with descriptive metadata; and the closure pattern hides binding-and-time semantics. Dijkstra additionally lands on the absence of a stated contract for `preview_fn`, with 'wrap in try-except if needed' standing in for real failure semantics. Torvalds catches non-runnable example payloads. Consensus verdict: NEEDS-WORK on examples and contract clarity before this documents a stable surface.
